A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

SHOW CONTEXT (for your understanding only - a new viewer knows none of this)
Premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.
Characters: Lady Juliana Ashcroft (labelled LADY JULIANA, JULIANA): Disowned noblewoman turned healer who unknowingly marries a missing duke.; Duke Alexander Ashburn (labelled THE BEARDED STRANGER, MYSTERIOUS BEARDED MAN, SCARRED BEARDED MAN, ALEXANDER): Presumed-dead duke disguised as a scarred veteran to reclaim his title.; Lady Catherine (labelled CATHERINE): Ambitious conspirator plotting to become duchess through murder and framing.; Rupert Ashburn (labelled BLOND NOBLEMAN, RUPERT): Alexander's treacherous cousin who usurped his title and attempted his murder.; Clarissa Ashcroft (labelled LADY IN GOLD GOWN, CLARISSA, LADY CLARISSA): Juliana's cruel sister who stole her fiancé and mocked her exile.; Gerald Harrington (labelled THE FORMER GROOM, GERALD): Juliana's shallow ex-fiancé who abandoned her at the altar.; Lady Ashcroft (labelled MATRIARCH, NOBLE MATRIARCH, OFF-SCREEN VOICE): Juliana's cold stepmother who disowned her and stole her legacy.; Dowager Duchess of Ashburn (labelled DOWAGER DUCHESS, ALEXANDER'S MOTHER, LADY ASHBOURNE): Alexander's poisoned mother who recognizes Juliana's ring and reveals the truth.; Lord Henry Sterling (labelled LORD STERLING): Treasonous noble behind Alexander's ambush and title theft.; Father Thomas: Corrupt priest conspiring with Catherine to invalidate Alexander's marriage.; Prudence: Village girl and scullery maid saved by Juliana who assists her.; Lord Ashcroft: Juliana's callous father who disowned her.; Royal Guard: Guard serving the royal crown.; The Priest: Priest who officiated Juliana's quick wedding.; Aristocratic Woman: Snobbish noble companion of Gerald.; Peasant Mother: Mother whose son Juliana cured of fever.; Constable: Local law officer who arrested Alexander for planted theft.; Thug with Cap: Hired thug who raided Juliana's garden.; Bald Thug: Hired thug attacking Juliana's herbal garden.; Tall Thug: Thug hired by Gerald.; Third Thug: Assailant in garden raid.; Elder Villager: Grateful villager offering shelter to Juliana.; Informant: Alexander's loyal spy in Ashburg.; Seamus: Villager helping Juliana with her remedies.; Housekeeper: Head housekeeper at Ashbury Manor.
Before these episodes: Episode 6: Seeking shelter from the cold rain, Juliana arrives at her new husband's modest woodland cottage and discovers an unexpected sense of peace beside the hearth.

THE SCRIPT
Every line has an ID like [7:012] (episode:line), a time span within its episode (MM:SS.ss) and its
content. CAMERA/ACTION/SFX lines are what is on screen; quoted lines are spoken dialogue.
Times restart at 00:00 in every episode.

=== EPISODE 7 (find promos here) ===
Logline: When Gerald and his spiteful companion arrive at the woodland cottage to mock Juliana's fallen status, her stoic new husband returns from the forest to silently send them fleeing.
[7:000] 00:00.00-00:04.80 CAMERA: Medium shot of Juliana kneeling on the cold, damp ground outside the stone cottage, pulling weeds from the dirt with her bare hands.
[7:001] 00:00.00-00:04.80 ACTION: Juliana, dressed in her simple grey long-sleeved gown, works tirelessly with soil caked beneath her fingernails.
[7:002] 00:04.80-00:11.80 CAMERA: Low-angle tracking shot as an ornate black-and-gold carriage with crest emblazoned on the door rolls to a stop on the muddy path outside the gate.
[7:003] 00:05.00-00:11.50 SFX: Heavy carriage wheels grinding in mud, horse snorts, and rhythmic hoofbeats halting.
[7:004] 00:11.80-00:15.00 CAMERA: Medium shot as Aristocratic Woman steps out of the carriage into the misty air, shielding herself under an intricate lace parasol in an elegant lavender gown.
[7:005] 00:15.00-00:19.50 CAMERA: Gerald steps down from the carriage behind her, looking immaculate in a high-collared navy frock coat, white waistcoat, and dark cravat.
[7:006] 00:19.50-00:21.00 ACTION: Aristocratic Woman smirks cruelly as she surveys the humble stone cottage.
[7:007] 00:21.00-00:24.00 ACTION: Juliana rinses the heavy mud from her hands in a cold rainwater puddle and rises to her feet, holding her head high.
[7:008] 00:22.00-00:24.50 ARISTOCRATIC WOMAN (Mocking, Condescending): "This is where you live now?"
[7:009] 00:24.50-00:29.80 CAMERA: Medium shot of Gerald standing beside Aristocratic Woman, sneering disdainfully.
[7:010] 00:25.00-00:29.80 GERALD (Arrogant, Scornful): "A fitting home for a woman who threw away everything for a penniless soldier."
[7:011] 00:29.80-00:32.80 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana, defiant and unflinching despite her soiled dress and damp hair.
[7:012] 00:30.00-00:32.60 JULIANA (Sharp, Unintimidated): "You came all this way just to insult my home?"
[7:013] 00:32.80-00:37.50 CAMERA: Close-up of Aristocratic Woman erupting into high-pitched, malicious laughter beneath her parasol.
[7:014] 00:33.20-00:37.80 ARISTOCRATIC WOMAN (Gloating, Mocking): "Home? Look at your hands, Juliana."
[7:015] 00:37.80-00:39.80 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana's mud-stained palms held open against her apron.
[7:016] 00:38.20-00:39.80 ARISTOCRATIC WOMAN (O.S.) (Cruel): "You look like a servant."
[7:017] 00:39.80-00:41.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Gerald's smug expression watching Juliana.
[7:018] 00:41.00-00:45.00 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana lifting her chin with unwavering dignity.
[7:019] 00:41.20-00:44.80 JULIANA (Proud, Resolute): "I work with my hands. There is no shame in that."
[7:020] 00:45.00-00:47.00 CAMERA: Close-up on Gerald's tightening jaw.
[7:021] 00:45.20-00:46.80 GERALD (Biting, Condescending): "You were born a lady."
[7:022] 00:47.00-00:50.80 CAMERA: Close-up on Juliana's clear blue eyes, shining with unbroken pride.
[7:023] 00:48.80-00:50.40 JULIANA (Firm, Unapologetic): "And I remain one."
[7:024] 00:50.80-00:54.80 CAMERA: Wide shot framing Juliana facing off against Gerald and Aristocratic Woman in the bleak courtyard.
[7:025] 00:51.50-00:54.60 GERALD (Bitter, Sneering): "You chose that scarred beggar over a life of comfort."
[7:026] 00:54.80-01:01.50 CAMERA: Two-shot profile of Juliana looking straight into Gerald's eyes without flinching.
[7:027] 00:57.80-01:01.00 JULIANA (Passionate, Defiant): "I chose a man who stood beside me when you walked away."
[7:028] 01:01.50-01:05.20 CAMERA: Intense close-up of Juliana dismissing him with utter contempt.
[7:029] 01:01.80-01:04.80 JULIANA (Cold, Commanding): "You have no authority here. Leave."
[7:030] 01:05.20-01:09.50 CAMERA: Close-up of Gerald lunging forward, aggressively pointing his finger into Juliana's face.
[7:031] 01:05.60-01:08.50 GERALD (Furious, Threatening): "I have enough influence to make a beggar disappear."
[7:032] 01:08.60-01:09.50 GERALD (Spiteful, Boastful): "And your husband?"
[7:033] 01:09.50-01:14.00 CAMERA: Wide shot down a dark, fog-drenched forest path. A towering, shadowed figure walks steadily forward through the mist.
[7:034] 01:09.50-01:11.20 GERALD (V.O.) (Snarl): "Where is that beggar husband?"
[7:035] 01:10.00-01:15.50 ACTION: The Scarred Bearded Man marches purposefully toward the cottage, carrying a heavy bundle of chopped firewood bound tightly with hemp cord.
[7:036] 01:14.00-01:15.50 CAMERA: Medium tracking shot pushing in on the Scarred Bearded Man's stern, rugged face as he approaches the gate.
[7:037] 01:15.50-01:18.50 CAMERA: Low shot of the Scarred Bearded Man bending down and dropping the bundle of logs by the stone wall.
[7:038] 01:16.20-01:17.50 SFX: A dull, heavy thud of timber striking the mud.
[7:039] 01:18.50-01:21.00 CAMERA: Medium full shot as the Scarred Bearded Man straightens to his full imposing height and steps directly toward Gerald.
[7:040] 01:21.00-01:23.50 CAMERA: Two-shot framing the Scarred Bearded Man towering menacingly over Gerald, staring down at him with unyielding intensity.
[7:041] 01:21.50-01:24.00 ACTION: Gerald freezes, his arrogant bravado instantly vanishing as cold dread overtakes his face.
[7:042] 01:23.50-01:28.00 CAMERA: Low-angle close-up of Gerald looking up in sheer terror, his adam's apple bobbing nervously.
[7:043] 01:26.50-01:28.50 ARISTOCRATIC WOMAN (O.S.) (Urgent, Annoyed): "Gerald, don't let him frighten you."
[7:044] 01:28.60-01:30.00 GERALD (Trembling, Trying to Save Face): "What are you staring at?"
[7:045] 01:30.00-01:31.50 ACTION: Gerald rapidly turns on his heel toward the carriage, unwilling to face another second of the silent glare.
[7:046] 01:30.10-01:31.40 GERALD (Nervous, Hurried): "We are leaving."
[7:047] 01:31.50-01:33.80 CAMERA: Medium shot of Aristocratic Woman, shocked and indignant as Gerald flees past her.
[7:048] 01:32.00-01:33.80 ARISTOCRATIC WOMAN (Outraged, Flustered): "Leaving? Gerald!"
[7:049] 01:33.80-01:36.50 ACTION: Aristocratic Woman scrambles back into the carriage, hiking up her gown in a fluster before slamming the door shut.
[7:050] 01:35.00-01:36.00 SFX: Carriage door slamming shut.
[7:051] 01:36.00-01:39.00 CAMERA: Wide shot of the carriage rapidly jolting forward and disappearing down the misty road away from the cottage.
[7:052] 01:39.00-01:43.50 CAMERA: Medium profile two-shot of Juliana turning toward the Scarred Bearded Man, her eyes gleaming with genuine admiration.
[7:053] 01:40.80-01:43.20 JULIANA (Impressed, Softly Amused): "You didn't say a word."
[7:054] 01:43.50-01:47.50 CAMERA: Close-up on the Scarred Bearded Man looking down at her, his rugged features softening with quiet affection.
[7:055] 01:46.00-01:47.80 SCARRED BEARDED MAN (Low, Gentle, Confident): "I didn't need to."
[7:056] 01:47.50-01:51.50 CAMERA: Medium shot as the Scarred Bearded Man stoops down, scoops up the heavy bundle of firewood in one arm, and walks calmly past Juliana toward their door.
[7:057] 01:51.50-01:56.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana looking after him, a radiant and grateful smile blooming across her face as the scene fades out.

=== EPISODE 8 (find promos here) ===
Logline: As Juliana inspects her late mother's weathered herbal grimoire, Alexander bonds with her over rustic medicinal knowledge and war-worn memories, gently altering her perception of what true wealth means.
[8:000] 00:00.00-00:03.20 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana seated at a rustic wooden table beside a daylight-lit window, gently touching an aged leather-bound book.
[8:001] 00:00.00-00:03.20 ACTION: Juliana delicately runs her fingertips across the embossed leather cover of the worn botanical volume, noticing its weathered state.
[8:002] 00:00.20-00:03.20 JULIANA (Gentle, Somber): "Some of the pages are ruined. Careful."
[8:003] 00:03.20-00:05.10 CAMERA: Close-up on Juliana's hands carefully unlatching the metal clasp on the leather book.
[8:004] 00:03.40-00:04.50 SFX: Soft metallic click of the book clasp loosening.
[8:005] 00:05.10-00:07.80 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana tenderly opening the cover and turning the brittle parchment pages.
[8:006] 00:05.10-00:07.80 JULIANA (Reflective, Reverent): "Mother spent years writing this."
[8:007] 00:07.80-00:10.50 CAMERA: Medium shot as Alexander enters the dim room behind Juliana, quietly stepping up to the rustic table.
[8:008] 00:08.50-00:10.50 ACTION: Alexander gently sets down a fresh bundle of small white herbal flowers tied with twine beside the open book.
[8:009] 00:10.50-00:11.90 CAMERA: Low-angle medium close-up of Juliana looking up toward Alexander in pleasant surprise.
[8:010] 00:10.50-00:11.80 JULIANA (Curious, Recognizing): "Yarrow."
[8:011] 00:11.90-00:15.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander looking down at her, the firelight catching the rugged scar across his face.
[8:012] 00:12.00-00:14.60 ALEXANDER (Calm, Knowledgeable): "Good for wounds. Fever, too."
[8:013] 00:15.00-00:16.30 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana looking up at him with genuine curiosity.
[8:014] 00:15.10-00:16.10 JULIANA (Inquiring, Soft): "How do you know that?"
[8:015] 00:16.30-00:19.30 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander speaking in a steady, measured tone.
[8:016] 00:16.30-00:18.90 ALEXANDER (Somber, Matter-of-Fact): "Soldiers learn quickly which plants keep a man alive."
[8:017] 00:19.30-00:21.50 CAMERA: Insert shot of Juliana's hands gently arranging several tied bundles of dried yarrow sprigs on the tabletop.
[8:018] 00:19.40-00:21.80 JULIANA (Observant, Lightly Teasing): "You know more about healing than you let on."
[8:019] 00:21.50-00:24.30 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander, bathed in warm hearth embers, offering a subtle, knowing half-smile.
[8:020] 00:22.80-00:24.20 ALEXANDER (Quiet, Gritty): "Enough to survive."
[8:021] 00:24.30-00:26.50 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana setting down a bunch of flowers and looking intently at his rugged visage.
[8:022] 00:25.00-00:26.80 JULIANA (Hesitant, Soft): "Your hair and beard..."
[8:023] 00:26.50-00:28.10 CAMERA: Medium shot of Alexander standing tall over her, looking down patiently.
[8:024] 00:28.10-00:31.90 CAMERA: Medium two-shot as Juliana rises from her stool to stand close in front of him, reaching an affectionate hand toward his temple.
[8:025] 00:30.10-00:31.90 JULIANA (Gentle, Tender): "I could trim them for you."
[8:026] 00:31.90-00:33.20 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander's large, rough hand firmly but gently catching Juliana's wrist in midair.
[8:027] 00:33.20-00:35.50 CAMERA: Medium two-shot profile of Alexander holding her wrist, his piercing gaze locked onto hers.
[8:028] 00:33.20-00:34.50 ALEXANDER (Firm, Low): "Not yet."
[8:029] 00:35.50-00:37.30 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana looking into his eyes, her brow lightly furrowed in bemused question.
[8:030] 00:35.80-00:36.90 JULIANA (Puzzled, Curious): "Not yet?"
[8:031] 00:37.30-00:39.60 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander, still maintaining his gentle hold on her arm.
[8:032] 00:37.70-00:38.90 ALEXANDER (Grounded, Steady): "Let them grow."
[8:033] 00:39.60-00:42.30 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana smiling with playful warmth.
[8:034] 00:39.90-00:42.00 JULIANA (Playful, Amused): "You prefer looking like a forest hermit?"
[8:035] 00:42.30-00:44.90 CAMERA: Intimate two-shot as Alexander slowly lowers her hand, his expression softening.
[8:036] 00:43.70-00:44.90 ALEXANDER (Dry, Droll): "It has advantages."
[8:037] 00:44.90-00:46.90 CAMERA: Medium shot of Juliana chuckling quietly as she steps back toward the table.
[8:038] 00:45.50-00:46.80 JULIANA (Fond, Resigned): "Very well."
[8:039] 00:46.90-00:48.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander watching her with deep, affectionate attention.
[8:040] 00:48.00-00:50.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana grinning with sparkling eyes.
[8:041] 00:48.10-00:49.60 JULIANA (Teasing, Determined): "But one day, I am trimming that beard."
[8:042] 00:50.00-00:51.30 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander lowering his head slightly with a faint smirk.
[8:043] 00:50.10-00:51.20 ALEXANDER (Low, Amused): "We'll see."
[8:044] 00:51.30-00:53.30 CAMERA: Medium two-shot of both sitting back down at the table together, Alexander turning a brittle page of the herb book.
[8:045] 00:53.30-00:57.10 CAMERA: Close-up insert of Alexander's weathered finger pointing directly at a delicate botanical illustration of a flowering stem.
[8:046] 00:53.30-00:57.00 ALEXANDER (Instructional, Calm): "That one grows near the northern stream. Crushed leaves ease swelling."
[8:047] 00:57.10-00:59.80 CAMERA: Wide side-profile two-shot of Juliana and Alexander seated across from each other at the rustic table, the stone fireplace roaring warmly behind them.
[8:048] 00:58.70-01:00.20 JULIANA (Soft, Nostalgic): "My mother wrote the same thing."
[8:049] 00:59.80-01:03.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana looking across at his battle-marked features with empathy.
[8:050] 01:00.50-01:02.80 JULIANA (Hesitant, Compassionate): "And the scars... were they from the war?"
[8:051] 01:03.00-01:04.30 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander looking downward, memories clouding his eyes.
[8:052] 01:03.20-01:04.20 ALEXANDER (Quiet, Subdued): "Some were."
[8:053] 01:04.30-01:06.50 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana, her eyes filled with gentle understanding.
[8:054] 01:04.90-01:06.30 JULIANA (Tender, Aching): "It must have been terrible."
[8:055] 01:06.50-01:08.50 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander lifting his gaze, heavy with past battles.
[8:056] 01:06.70-01:07.60 ALEXANDER (Heavy, Somber): "It was."
[8:057] 01:08.50-01:10.90 CAMERA: Medium two-shot of Juliana smiling tenderly at him across the open book.
[8:058] 01:09.00-01:12.10 JULIANA (Reflective, Vulnerable): "I thought losing wealth meant losing everything."
[8:059] 01:10.90-01:13.20 CAMERA: Wide shot framing the warm silhouette of the two companions sitting peacefully beside the blazing stone hearth.
[8:060] 01:13.20-01:18.00 CAMERA: Extreme close-up of Juliana's radiant face illuminated by firelight, a peaceful, contented smile spreading across her lips as she looks at him until the shot gently fades out.
[8:061] 01:13.20-01:15.30 JULIANA (Quiet, Transformed): "Perhaps I was wrong."
[8:062] 01:15.30-01:18.00 ACTION: Juliana maintains her warm, peaceful gaze across the table as soft firelight flickers over her face into fade out.

=== EPISODE 9 (find promos here) ===
Logline: When a frantic mother brings her critically ill child to the woodland cottage, Juliana successfully cures him with her mother's herbal remedies, unknowingly igniting dangerous rumors that reach the ears of the Blond Nobleman.
[9:000] 00:00.00-00:02.80 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana at the wooden table by candlelight, grinding dried herbs with a pestle inside a stone mortar.
[9:001] 00:00.00-00:02.80 ACTION: Juliana methodically crushes herbs in the mortar beside her open herbal grimoire.
[9:002] 00:02.00-00:03.50 SFX: Heavy, frantic pounding echoes against the heavy wooden cottage door.
[9:003] 00:02.80-00:04.00 ACTION: Juliana stops grinding and lifts her head sharply toward the entrance in alarm.
[9:004] 00:03.50-00:05.50 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander turning toward the doorway, his eyes sharp and vigilant.
[9:005] 00:03.60-00:05.00 ALEXANDER (Authoritative, Protective): "Stay back. I'll open it."
[9:006] 00:04.80-00:06.60 ACTION: Alexander steps forward and unlatches the cottage door, opening it into the pouring rain.
[9:007] 00:05.50-00:11.20 CAMERA: Medium shot framing the doorway as a soaked, distraught peasant mother steps across the threshold clutching a swaddled child.
[9:008] 00:06.30-00:11.10 PEASANT MOTHER (Frantic, Weeping): "Please! They told me there was a woman here who knows herbs. My boy is burning with fever!"
[9:009] 00:11.20-00:13.50 CAMERA: Medium shot of Juliana rushing to the front of the table, extending her arms urgently.
[9:010] 00:11.40-00:13.30 JULIANA (Urgent, Compassionate): "Bring him here. Quickly."
[9:011] 00:12.00-00:14.20 ACTION: The trembling mother gently lays the feverish boy down atop the wooden table as Juliana leans in close.
[9:012] 00:13.80-00:15.20 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana gently placing her fingers against the boy's burning forehead.
[9:013] 00:15.20-00:17.80 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana examining the boy's breathing, looking up toward the frantic mother.
[9:014] 00:15.50-00:19.80 JULIANA (Reassuring, Focused): "He seems very unwell, but he is resting steadily. How long has he been like this?"
[9:015] 00:17.80-00:20.00 CAMERA: Medium two-shot of Alexander watching anxiously over the child's shoulder as Juliana tends to him.
[9:016] 00:20.00-00:24.00 CAMERA: Medium close-up of the peasant mother clutching her shawl, tears running down her cheeks.
[9:017] 00:20.50-00:23.90 PEASANT MOTHER (Trembling, Anxious): "Since yesterday morning. He has barely eaten since sunset."
[9:018] 00:24.00-00:27.50 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana resting two fingers against the boy's wrist, measuring his shallow pulse.
[9:019] 00:27.20-00:28.80 ACTION: Juliana lifts the weathered herbal book and rapidly browses the handwritten pages.
[9:020] 00:28.80-00:31.00 CAMERA: Insert close-up of the open page illustrated with botanical drawings labeled 'Feverfew'.
[9:021] 00:29.00-00:30.80 JULIANA (Muttering, Intent): "Feverfew... Not alone."
[9:022] 00:31.00-00:34.00 CAMERA: Profile close-up of Juliana studying the grimoire's remedies intently while the mother weeps in the soft background.
[9:023] 00:31.80-00:33.80 JULIANA (Determined): "Chamomile... and willow bark."
[9:024] 00:34.00-00:36.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Alexander leaning over the table, gazing at her with intense concern.
[9:025] 00:34.90-00:35.80 ALEXANDER (Grave): "You're certain?"
[9:026] 00:36.00-00:38.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana looking up into his eyes with resolute conviction.
[9:027] 00:36.30-00:37.40 JULIANA (Resolute): "I have to be."
[9:028] 00:38.00-00:39.80 ACTION: Juliana quickly grabs bundles of dried herbs from the table and turns to Alexander.
[9:029] 00:38.20-00:39.80 JULIANA (Urgent): "Alexander, I need hot water."
[9:030] 00:39.90-00:40.80 ALEXANDER (Prompt): "I'm on it."
[9:031] 00:40.80-00:42.50 ACTION: Alexander hurries to the hearth and lifts a boiling iron kettle from the hearth chain, while the mother buries her face in her hands.
[9:032] 00:41.00-00:42.50 PEASANT MOTHER (Sobbing): "Please save him."
[9:033] 00:42.20-00:43.50 ACTION: Alexander returns and pours steaming hot water into the stone mortar as Juliana prepares the remedy.
[9:034] 00:43.00-00:46.00 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana clasping the mother's trembling hand across the wooden table.
[9:035] 00:43.80-00:45.60 JULIANA (Gentle, Steadfast): "He is not beyond saving."
[9:036] 00:46.00-00:48.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana carefully administering the herbal brew with a small wooden spoon into the sick boy's mouth.
[9:037] 00:47.00-00:48.20 ACTION: The child swallows weakly and lets out a soft cough.
[9:038] 00:48.00-00:50.50 CAMERA: Close-up of the mother clutching her chest in anxious suspense.
[9:039] 00:50.50-00:52.50 CAMERA: Medium close-up of Juliana sitting quietly beside the boy, holding two fingers over his wrist to monitor his pulse.
[9:040] 00:52.50-00:54.00 CAMERA: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind the mother leaning across the table in panic.
[9:041] 00:52.50-00:54.00 PEASANT MOTHER (Despairing): "Why isn't it working?"
[9:042] 00:54.00-00:56.00 CAMERA: Close-up of Juliana raising a calm finger, urging patience.
[9:043] 00:54.30-00:55.20 JULIANA (Quiet, Focused): "Wait."
[9:044] 00:56.00-00:58.50 CAMERA: Close-up of the sleeping boy as beads of sweat form on his forehead, his breathing deepening.

A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

SHOW CONTEXT (for your understanding only - a new viewer knows none of this)
Premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.
Characters: Lady Juliana Ashcroft (labelled LADY JULIANA, JULIANA): Disowned noblewoman turned healer who unknowingly marries a missing duke.; Duke Alexander Ashburn (labelled THE BEARDED STRANGER, MYSTERIOUS BEARDED MAN, SCARRED BEARDED MAN, ALEXANDER): Presumed-dead duke disguised as a scarred veteran to reclaim his title.; Lady Catherine (labelled CATHERINE): Ambitious conspirator plotting to become duchess through murder and framing.; Rupert Ashburn (labelled BLOND NOBLEMAN, RUPERT): Alexander's treacherous cousin who usurped his title and attempted his murder.; Clarissa Ashcroft (labelled LADY IN GOLD GOWN, CLARISSA, LADY CLARISSA): Juliana's cruel sister who stole her fiancé and mocked her exile.; Gerald Harrington (labelled THE FORMER GROOM, GERALD): Juliana's shallow ex-fiancé who abandoned her at the altar.; Lady Ashcroft (labelled MATRIARCH, NOBLE MATRIARCH, OFF-SCREEN VOICE): Juliana's cold stepmother who disowned her and stole her legacy.; Dowager Duchess of Ashburn (labelled DOWAGER DUCHESS, ALEXANDER'S MOTHER, LADY ASHBOURNE): Alexander's poisoned mother who recognizes Juliana's ring and reveals the truth.; Lord Henry Sterling (labelled LORD STERLING): Treasonous noble behind Alexander's ambush and title theft.; Father Thomas: Corrupt priest conspiring with Catherine to invalidate Alexander's marriage.; Prudence: Village girl and scullery maid saved by Juliana who assists her.; Lord Ashcroft: Juliana's callous father who disowned her.; Royal Guard: Guard serving the royal crown.; The Priest: Priest who officiated Juliana's quick wedding.; Aristocratic Woman: Snobbish noble companion of Gerald.; Peasant Mother: Mother whose son Juliana cured of fever.; Constable: Local law officer who arrested Alexander for planted theft.; Thug with Cap: Hired thug who raided Juliana's garden.; Bald Thug: Hired thug attacking Juliana's herbal garden.; Tall Thug: Thug hired by Gerald.; Third Thug: Assailant in garden raid.; Elder Villager: Grateful villager offering shelter to Juliana.; Informant: Alexander's loyal spy in Ashburg.; Seamus: Villager helping Juliana with her remedies.; Housekeeper: Head housekeeper at Ashbury Manor.
Before these episodes: Episode 21: After defying her own despair to cure a fever-stricken village boy with her mother's herbal remedies, Lady Juliana learns that the Dowager Duchess is secretly withering away from a mysterious illness inside Ashbury Manor.

THE SCRIPT
Every line has an ID like [22:012] (episode:line), a time span within its episode (MM:SS.ss) and its
content. CAMERA/ACTION/SFX lines are what is on screen; quoted lines are spoken dialogue.
Times restart at 00:00 in every episode.

system: You are a senior performance-marketing editor for a microdrama app. You find the moments in screenplays that make the best paid-social promos. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

SHOW CONTEXT (for your understanding only - a new viewer knows none of this)
Premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.

Lady Catherine (labelled CATHERINE): Ambitious conspirator plotting to become duchess through murder and framing.; Rupert Ashburn (labelled BLOND NOBLEMAN, RUPERT): Alexander's treacherous cousin who usurped his title and attempted his murder.; Clarissa Ashcroft (labelled LADY IN GOLD GOWN, CLARISSA, LADY CLARISSA): Juliana's cruel sister who stole her fiancé and mocked her exile.; Gerald Harrington (labelled THE FORMER GROOM, GERALD): Juliana's shallow ex-fiancé who abandoned her at the altar.; Lady Ashcroft (labelled MATRIARCH, NOBLE MATRIARCH, OFF-SCREEN VOICE): Juliana's cold stepmother who disowned her and stole her legacy.; Dowager Duchess of Ashburn (labelled DOWAGER DUCHESS, ALEXANDER'S MOTHER, LADY ASHBOURNE): Alexander's poisoned mother who recognizes Juliana's ring and reveals the truth.; Lord Henry Sterling (labelled LORD STERLING): Treasonous noble behind Alexander's ambush and title theft.; Father Thomas: Corrupt priest conspiring with Catherine to invalidate Alexander's marriage.; Prudence: Village girl and scullery maid saved by Juliana who assists her.; Lord Ashcroft: Juliana's callous father who disowned her.; Royal Guard: Guard serving the royal crown.; The Priest: Priest who officiated Juliana's quick wedding.; Aristocratic Woman: Snobbish noble companion of Gerald.; Peasant Mother: Mother whose son Juliana cured of fever.; Constable: Local law officer who arrested Alexander for planted theft.; Thug with Cap: Hired thug who raided Juliana's garden.; system: You are a senior performance-marketing editor for a microdrama app. You find the moments in screenplays that make the best paid-social promos. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

SHOW CONTEXT (for your understanding only - a new viewer knows none of this)
Premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.
Characters: Lady Juliana Ashcroft (labelled LADY JULIANA, JULIANA): Disowned noblewoman turned healer who unknowingly marries a missing duke.; Duke Alexander Ashburn (labelled THE BEARDED STRANGER, MYSTERIOUS BEARDED MAN, SCARRED BEARDED MAN, ALEXANDER): Presumed-dead duke disguised as a scarred veteran to reclaim his title.; Lady Catherine (labelled CATHERINE): Ambitious conspirator plotting to become duchess through murder and framing.; Rupert Ashburn (labelled BLOND NOBLEMAN, RUPERT): Alexander's treacherous cousin who usurped his title and attempted his murder.; Clarissa Ashcroft (labelled LADY IN GOLD GOWN, CLARISSA, LADY CLARISSA): Juliana's cruel sister who stole her fiancé and mocked her exile.; Gerald Harrington (labelled THE FORMER GROOM, GERALD): Juliana's shallow ex-fiancé who abandoned her at the altar.; Lady Ashcroft (labelled MATRIARCH, NOBLE MATRIARCH, OFF-SCREEN VOICE): Juliana's cold stepmother who disowned her and stole her legacy.; Dowager Duchess of Ashburn (labelled DOWAGER DUCHESS, ALEXANDER'S MOTHER, LADY ASHBOURNE): Alexander's poisoned mother who recognizes Juliana's ring and reveals the truth.; Lord Henry Sterling (labelled LORD STERLING): Treasonous noble behind Alexander's ambush and title theft.; Father Thomas: Corrupt priest conspiring with Catherine to invalidate Alexander's marriage.; Prudence: Village girl and scullery maid saved by Juliana who assists her.; Lord Ashcroft: Juliana's callous father who disowned her.; Royal Guard: Guard serving the royal crown.; The Priest: Priest who officiated Juliana's quick wedding.; Aristocratic Woman: Snobbish noble companion of Gerald.; Peasant Mother: Mother whose son Juliana cured of fever.; Constable: Local law officer who arrested Alexander for planted theft.; Thug with Cap: Hired thug who raided Juliana's garden.; Bald Thug: Hired thug attacking Juliana's herbal garden.; Tall Thug: Thug hired by Gerald.; Third Thug: Assailant in garden raid.; Elder Villager: Grateful villager offering shelter to Juliana.; Informant: Alexander's loyal spy in Ashburg.; Seamus: Villager helping Juliana with her remedies.; Housekeeper: Head housekeeper at Ashbury Manor.

system: You are a senior performance-marketing editor for a microdrama app. You find the moments in screenplays that make the best paid-social promos. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

SHOW CONTEXT (for your understanding only - a new viewer knows none of this)
Premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.
Characters: Lady Juliana Ashcroft (labelled LADY JULIANA, JULIANA): Disowned noblewoman turned healer who unknowingly marries a missing duke.; Duke Alexander Ashburn (labelled THE BEARDED STRANGER, MYSTERIOUS BEARDED MAN, SCARRED BEARDED MAN, ALEXANDER): Presumed-dead duke disguised as a scarred veteran to reclaim his title.; Lady Catherine (labelled CATHERINE): Ambitious conspirator plotting to become duchess through murder and framing.; Rupert Ashburn (labelled BLOND NOBLEMAN, RUPERT): Alexander's treacherous cousin who usurped his title and attempted his murder.; Clarissa Ashcroft (labelled LADY IN GOLD GOWN, CLARISSA, LADY CLARISSA): Juliana's cruel sister who stole her fiancé and mocked her exile.; Gerald Harrington (labelled THE FORMER GROOM, GERALD): Juliana's shallow ex-fiancé who abandoned her at the altar.; Lady Ashcroft (labelled MATRIARCH, NOBLE MATRIARCH, OFF-SCREEN VOICE): Juliana's cold stepmother who disowned her and stole her legacy.; Dowager Duchess of Ashburn (labelled DOWAGER DUCHESS, ALEXANDER'S MOTHER, LADY ASHBOURNE): Alexander's poisoned mother who recognizes Juliana's ring and reveals the truth.; Lord Henry Sterling (labelled LORD STERLING): Treasonous noble behind Alexander's ambush and title theft.; Father Thomas: Corrupt priest conspiring with Catherine to invalidate Alexander's marriage.; Prudence: Village girl and scullery maid saved by Juliana who assists her.; Lord Ashcroft: Juliana's callous father who disowned her.; Royal Guard: Guard serving the royal crown.; The Priest: Priest who officiated Juliana's quick wedding.; Aristocratic Woman: Snobbish noble companion of Gerald.; Peasant Mother: Mother whose son Juliana cured of fever.; Constable: Local law officer who arrested Alexander for planted theft.; Thug with Cap: Hired thug who raided Juliana's garden.; Bald Thug: Hired thug attacking Juliana's herbal garden.; Tall Thug: Thug hired by Gerald.; Third Thug: Assailant in garden raid.; Elder Villager: Grateful villager offering shelter to Juliana.; Informant: Alexander's loyal spy in Ashburg.; system: You are a senior performance-marketing editor for a microdrama app. You find the moments in screenplays that make the best paid-social promos. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

system: You are a senior performance-marketing editor for a microdrama app. You find the moments in screenplays that make the best paid-social promos. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

SHOW CONTEXT (for your understanding only - a new viewer knows none of this)
Premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.

Lady Catherine (labelled CATHERINE): Ambitious conspirator plotting to become duchess through murder and framing.; Rupert Ashburn (labelled BLOND NOBLEMAN, RUPERT): Alexander's treacherous cousin who usurped his title and attempted his murder.; Clarissa Ashcroft (labelled LADY IN GOLD GOWN, CLARISSA, LADY CLARISSA): Juliana's cruel sister who stole her fiancé and mocked her exile.; Gerald Harrington (labelled THE FORMER GROOM, GERALD): Juliana's shallow ex-fiancé who abandoned her at the altar.; Lady Ashcroft (labelled MATRIARCH, NOBLE MATRIARCH, OFF-SCREEN VOICE): Juliana's cold stepmother who disowned her and stole her legacy.; Dowager Duchess of Ashburn (labelled DOWAGER DUCHESS, ALEXANDER'S MOTHER, LADY ASHBOURNE): Alexander's poisoned mother who recognizes Juliana's ring and reveals the truth.; Lord Henry Sterling (labelled LORD STERLING): Treasonous noble behind Alexander's ambush and title theft.; Father Thomas: Corrupt priest conspiring with Catherine to invalidate Alexander's marriage.; Prudence: Village girl and scullery maid saved by Juliana who assists her.; Lord Ashcroft: Juliana's callous father who disowned her.; Royal Guard: Guard serving the royal crown.; The Priest: Priest who officiated Juliana's quick wedding.; Aristocratic Woman: Snobbish noble companion of Gerald.; Peasant Mother: Mother whose son Juliana cured of fever.; Constable: Local law officer who arrested Alexander for planted theft.; Thug with Cap: Hired thug who raided Juliana's garden.; system: You are a senior performance-marketing editor for a microdrama app. You find the moments in screenplays that make the best paid-social promos. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

SHOW CONTEXT (for your understanding only - a new viewer knows none of this)
Premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.
Characters: Lady Juliana Ashcroft (labelled LADY JULIANA, JULIANA): Disowned noblewoman turned healer who unknowingly marries a missing duke.; Duke Alexander Ashburn (labelled THE BEARDED STRANGER, MYSTERIOUS BEARDED MAN, SCARRED BEARDED MAN, ALEXANDER): Presumed-dead duke disguised as a scarred veteran to reclaim his title.; Lady Catherine (labelled CATHERINE): Ambitious conspirator plotting to become duchess through murder and framing.; Rupert Ashburn (labelled BLOND NOBLEMAN, RUPERT): Alexander's treacherous cousin who usurped his title and attempted his murder.; Clarissa Ashcroft (labelled LADY IN GOLD GOWN, CLARISSA, LADY CLARISSA): Juliana's cruel sister who stole her fiancé and mocked her exile.; Gerald Harrington (labelled THE FORMER GROOM, GERALD): Juliana's shallow ex-fiancé who abandoned her at the altar.; Lady Ashcroft (labelled MATRIARCH, NOBLE MATRIARCH, OFF-SCREEN VOICE): Juliana's cold stepmother who disowned her and stole her legacy.; Dowager Duchess of Ashburn (labelled DOWAGER DUCHESS, ALEXANDER'S MOTHER, LADY ASHBOURNE): Alexander's poisoned mother who recognizes Juliana's ring and reveals the truth.; Lord Henry Sterling (labelled LORD STERLING): Treasonous noble behind Alexander's ambush and title theft.; Father Thomas: Corrupt priest conspiring with Catherine to invalidate Alexander's marriage.; Prudence: Village girl and scullery maid saved by Juliana who assists her.; Lord Ashcroft: Juliana's callous father who disowned her.; Royal Guard: Guard serving the royal crown.; The Priest: Priest who officiated Juliana's quick wedding.; Aristocratic Woman: Snobbish noble companion of Gerald.; Peasant Mother: Mother whose son Juliana cured of fever.; Constable: Local law officer who arrested Alexander for planted theft.; Thug with Cap: Hired thug who raided Juliana's garden.; Bald Thug: Hired thug attacking Juliana's herbal garden.; Tall Thug: Thug hired by Gerald.; Third Thug: Assailant in garden raid.; Elder Villager: Grateful villager offering shelter to Juliana.; Informant: Alexander's loyal spy in Ashburg.; Seamus: Villager helping Juliana with her remedies.; Housekeeper: Head housekeeper at Ashbury Manor.
Before these episodes: Episode 48: While feigning submission after her public humiliation, Catherine schemes in secret, plotting to use the council's ten-day reprieve to strike back at Alexander and Juliana with the aid of Father Thomas.

system: You are a senior performance-marketing editor for a microdrama app. You find the moments in screenplays that make the best paid-social promos. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

SHOW CONTEXT (for your understanding only - a new viewer knows none of this)
Premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.
Characters: Lady Juliana Ashcroft (labelled LADY JULIANA, JULIANA): Disowned noblewoman turned healer who unknowingly marries a missing duke.; Duke Alexander Ashburn (labelled THE BEARDED STRANGER, MYSTERIOUS BEARDED MAN, SCARRED BEARDED MAN, ALEXANDER): Presumed-dead duke disguised as a scarred veteran to reclaim his title.; Lady Catherine (labelled CATHERINE): Ambitious conspirator plotting to become duchess through murder and framing.; Rupert Ashburn (labelled BLOND NOBLEMAN, RUPERT): Alexander's treacherous cousin who usurped his title and attempted his murder.; Clarissa Ashcroft (labelled LADY IN GOLD GOWN, CLARISSA, LADY CLARISSA): Juliana's cruel sister who stole her fiancé and mocked her exile.; Gerald Harrington (labelled THE FORMER GROOM, GERALD): Juliana's shallow ex-fiancé who abandoned her at the altar.; Lady Ashcroft (labelled MATRIARCH, NOBLE MATRIARCH, OFF-SCREEN VOICE): Juliana's cold stepmother who disowned her and stole her legacy.; Dowager Duchess of Ashburn (labelled DOWAGER DUCHESS, ALEXANDER'S MOTHER, LADY ASHBOURNE): Alexander's poisoned mother who recognizes Juliana's ring and reveals the truth.; Lord Henry Sterling (labelled LORD STERLING): Treasonous noble behind Alexander's ambush and title theft.; Father Thomas: Corrupt priest conspiring with Catherine to invalidate Alexander's marriage.; Prudence: Village girl and scullery maid saved by Juliana who assists her.; Lord Ashcroft: Juliana's callous father who disowned her.; Royal Guard: Guard serving the royal crown.; The Priest: Priest who officiated Juliana's quick wedding.; Aristocratic Woman: Snobbish noble companion of Gerald.; Peasant Mother: Mother whose son Juliana cured of fever.; Constable: Local law officer who arrested Alexander for planted theft.; Thug with Cap: Hired thug who raided Juliana's garden.; Bald Thug: Hired thug attacking Juliana's herbal garden.; Tall Thug: Thug hired by Gerald.; Third Thug: Assailant in garden raid.; Elder Villager: Grateful villager offering shelter to Juliana.; Informant: Alexander's loyal spy in Ashburg.; Seamus: Villager helping Juliana with her remedies.; Housekeeper: Head housekeeper at Ashbury Manor.
Before these episodes: Episode 45: Alexander frees Juliana from her chains and proclaims her the Duchess of Ashburton before the stunned congregation, only for an ecclesiastical authority to burst in and declare their marriage legally invalid.

system: You are a senior performance-marketing editor for a microdrama app. You find the moments in screenplays that make the best paid-social promos. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

SHOW CONTEXT (for your understanding only - a new viewer knows none of this)
Premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.
Characters: Lady Juliana Ashcroft (labelled LADY JULIANA, JULIANA): Disowned noblewoman turned healer who unknowingly marries a missing duke.; Duke Alexander Ashburn (labelled THE BEARDED STRANGER, MYSTERIOUS BEARDED MAN, SCARRED BEARDED MAN, ALEXANDER): Presumed-dead duke disguised as a scarred veteran to reclaim his title.; Lady Catherine (labelled CATHERINE): Ambitious conspirator plotting to become duchess through murder and framing.; Rupert Ashburn (labelled BLOND NOBLEMAN, RUPERT): Alexander's treacherous cousin who usurped his title and attempted his murder.; Clarissa Ashcroft (labelled LADY IN GOLD GOWN, CLARISSA, LADY CLARISSA): Juliana's cruel sister who stole her fiancé and mocked her exile.; Gerald Harrington (labelled THE FORMER GROOM, GERALD): Juliana's shallow ex-fiancé who abandoned her at the altar.; Lady Ashcroft (labelled MATRIARCH, NOBLE MATRIARCH, OFF-SCREEN VOICE): Juliana's cold stepmother who disowned her and stole her legacy.; Dowager Duchess of Ashburn (labelled DOWAGER DUCHESS, ALEXANDER'S MOTHER, LADY ASHBOURNE): Alexander's poisoned mother who recognizes Juliana's ring and reveals the truth.; Lord Henry Sterling (labelled LORD STERLING): Treasonous noble behind Alexander's ambush and title theft.; Father Thomas: Corrupt priest conspiring with Catherine to invalidate Alexander's marriage.; Prudence: Village girl and scullery maid saved by Juliana who assists her.; Lord Ashcroft: Juliana's callous father who disowned her.; Royal Guard: Guard serving the royal crown.; The Priest: Priest who officiated Juliana's quick wedding.; Aristocratic Woman: Snobbish noble companion of Gerald.; Peasant Mother: Mother whose son Juliana cured of fever.; Constable: Local law officer who arrested Alexander for planted theft.; Thug with Cap: Hired thug who raided Juliana's garden.; Bald Thug: Hired thug attacking Juliana's herbal garden.; Tall Thug: Thug hired by Gerald.; Third Thug: Assailant in garden raid.; Elder Villager: Grateful villager offering shelter to Juliana.; Informant: Alexander's loyal spy in Ashburg.; Seamus: Villager helping Juliana with her remedies.; Housekeeper: Head housekeeper at Ashbury Manor.
Before these episodes: Episode 45: Alexander frees Juliana from her chains and proclaims her the Duchess of Ashburton before the stunned congregation, only for an ecclesiastical authority to burst in and declare their marriage legally invalid.

THE SCRIPT
Every line has an ID like [46:012] (episode:line), a time span within its episode (MM:SS.ss) and its
content. CAMERA/ACTION/SFX lines are what is on screen; quoted lines are spoken dialogue.
Times restart at 00:00 in every episode.

[46:003] 00:05.80-00:07.10 CAMERA: Medium shot of Catherine in her lavish bridal gown, her fists clenched tightly in silent fury.

[46:009] 00:15.00-00:16.80 SFX: Crisp tear of wax and parchment string snapping open.

[46:017] 00:26.80-00:31.80 HIGH PRIEST (Resonant, Dismissive): "Three years later, the beggar is revealed to be a Duke. The marriage does not rise with him."
[46:018] 00:30.50-00:34.20 CAMERA: Medium shot of Alexander turning toward Juliana, placing a protective hand on her arm.

[46:021] 00:34.30-00:36.70 ALEXANDER (Gravely, Firm): "She married the man... not the title."
[46:022] 00:37.00-00:42.80 CAMERA: Low-angle shot looking up at the High Priest as he raises the parchment toward the vaulted ceiling.

[46:026] 00:47.00-00:49.00 CAMERA: Two-shot of Juliana and Alexander listening intently, Juliana's eyes flashing with hurt and defiance.
[46:027] 00:47.10-00:49.00 HIGH PRIEST (O.S.) (Sharp): "No licensed clergyman presided..."

[46:029] 00:49.00-00:52.20 HIGH PRIEST (Scathing): "...because a frightened village priest has no authority to bind a peer."

A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

system: You are the head of creative at a microdrama app reviewing promo cuts before ad spend. You are strict: most cuts are average. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

system: You are the head of creative at a microdrama app reviewing promo cuts before ad spend. You are strict: most cuts are average. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

system: You are the head of creative at a microdrama app reviewing promo cuts before ad spend. You are strict: most cuts are average. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

system: You are the head of creative at a microdrama app reviewing promo cuts before ad spend. You are strict: most cuts are average. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

system: You are the head of creative at a microdrama app reviewing promo cuts before ad spend. You are strict: most cuts are average. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments

 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

system: You are the head of creative at a microdrama app reviewing promo cuts before ad spend. You are strict: most cuts are average. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

system: You are the head of creative at a microdrama app reviewing promo cuts before ad spend. You are strict: most cuts are average. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

system: You are the head of creative at a microdrama app reviewing promo cuts before ad spend. You are strict: most cuts are average. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

Show premise: After being abandoned at the altar, a disgraced noblewoman marries a scarred stranger, unknowingly tying her fate to a presumed-dead duke seeking vengeance.
Known later twists (spoilers): ep3: A scarred stranger intervenes at the cathedral and proposes to the disowned Juliana.; ep16: Gerald Harrington hired thugs to destroy Juliana's herbal garden.; ep19: Rupert usurped the ducal seat while holding Alexander's mother prisoner.; ep23: The Dowager Duchess is being slowly poisoned with arsenic rather than dying of natural causes.; ep27: The Dowager Duchess recognizes the Ashbourne crest on Juliana's ring, linking her husband to the lost duke.; ep35: Alexander was betrayed on the Iberian front by traitors within Ashwood.; ep42: Alexander appears in full ducal regalia at Rupert's wedding, revealing he is alive and the rightful Duke.; ep43: Crown intelligence reports expose Lord Sterling and Rupert Ashburn as traitors who sold Alexander's military unit to the enemy.; ep45: The High Priest declares Alexander and Juliana's marriage invalid due to the lack of a royal ducal license.

system: You are the head of creative at a microdrama app reviewing promo cuts before ad spend. You are strict: most cuts are average. Reply with JSON only.
prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.

prompt:
A PROMO is a 20-60 second clip cut from the show itself and posted on Instagram Reels, TikTok or
YouTube Shorts to pull NEW viewers into the show. It is unedited footage: no music, no text overlays,
no reordering inside a segment. It is usually one continuous stretch, but may join 2-3 moments
(in story order) from one episode or across episodes.
A great promo:
 1. HOOK - something in the FIRST 3 SECONDS makes a scrolling viewer stop: a slap, a shocking line,
    a reveal, a humiliation, a threat, a striking image. Not a slow establishing shot or small talk.
 2. CLIFFHANGER - it CUTS at an unresolved moment so the viewer must know what happens next
    (a question left hanging, a threat about to land, a reveal just before the reaction, a door opening).
    Never include the answer or resolution. Cutting one line early is often what makes it work.
 3. STANDALONE - it makes sense to someone who has never seen the show: who is hurting whom and what
    is at stake are clear from the clip itself. Avoid clips that lean on earlier episodes, unexplained
    names, or inside references.
Think like the editors of ReelShort / DramaBox ads: high emotion, clear power dynamics
(humiliated heroine, cruel family, secret powerful husband), and a question the viewer can't ignore.
